title: What if a Carrington-level solar storm hit tonight?
premise: A solar storm as strong as the 1859 Carrington Event hits modern, electrified Earth.

intro.title: What if a *solar storm* hit tonight?
intro.subtitle: BASED ON THE 1859 CARRINGTON EVENT

beats.caption: A massive eruption blasts off the Sun, aimed straight at Earth.

tooltip.label: REAL EVENT
tooltip.text: In 1859, a storm like this reached Earth in about 17.6 hours.

beats.caption: We'd have less than a day to prepare.
The storm hits. Auroras blaze across the whole sky.

tooltip.label: REAL EVENT
tooltip.text: In 1859, auroras were seen as far south as the Caribbean.

beats.caption: Even places that never see the northern lights would see them now.
Then power grids start to overload.

tooltip.label: REAL EVENT
tooltip.text: A much weaker storm in 1989 knocked out power for six million people in Quebec for nine hours.

beats.caption: Satellites get blasted with radiation. GPS and radio signals scramble.
Huge transformers are hard to replace. Some repairs could take months.

tooltip.label: FACT
tooltip.text: The Sun is near the peak of its 11-year cycle, when big storms are most likely.

beats.caption: It's not if a storm like this hits again. It's when.
